questions.stem: How does this page say Java reads the expression `!a == b`?

options.text: As `!(a == b)`: the comparison binds first, then the negation applies
options.says: The page says the unary ! binds tighter than all the others.

options.text: As a compile error: mixing these two operators needs explicit parentheses
options.says: The page reads the expression as valid and says how it is grouped.

options.text: As `(!a) == b`: the negation binds first, then the comparison applies
options.says: The page's own example says !a == b means (!a) == b.

questions.stem: Which type does this page suggest for money arithmetic, such as prices?

options.text: `double`, since its 64 bits give prices plenty of precision
options.says: The page warns that floating-point arithmetic can bring precision errors.

options.text: `BigDecimal`, since it keeps decimal amounts free of rounding
options.says: The page names BigDecimal for precise decimal calculations, especially financial ones.

options.text: `float`, since prices seldom need more than seven digits
options.says: The page warns that floating-point arithmetic can bring precision errors; it names BigDecimal instead.
